output.analysis_scope_reason: A daily equity-and-rates transmission explainer ahead of the scheduled jobs report, using dated background rather than analysing an unreleased outcome or replacing the separate event dossier.
output.editorial_thesis: A weaker jobs report can reduce the interest-rate pressure on US equity valuations while also weakening the earnings outlook. The useful question is which channel dominates: a lower Treasury yield alone cannot answer it. Use September employment, wages and revisions as dated background and the Treasury series through 4 November as the rate backdrop; distinguish a conditional mechanism from an observed market reaction.
output.countercase: Orderly labour cooling alongside continued hiring and moderating wage growth could ease rate pressure without materially damaging earnings. Conversely, softer employment and downward revisions could signal demand weakness, while sticky wages could limit any rate relief. Neither a weak payroll headline nor a falling 10-year yield establishes the equity outcome; risk premiums and company profits also matter.
proposed_section_headings: A lower yield is only half the equity story
The last jobs report was weak, but not uniform
Three checks beyond the payroll headline

charts.question: Which non-overlapping employer groups contributed to September’s small payroll gain?
charts.why_useful: Shows why a single headline is an incomplete read on labour demand: private goods and private services added jobs while government employment fell. It supports the earnings-side question without claiming a recession or forecasting October.
charts.placement_after: The last jobs report was weak, but not uniform

data_spec.source_series: Employment Situation Table B-1, seasonally adjusted employment: Total nonfarm, Total private, Goods-producing, Private service-providing; August and September 2026 levels and September monthly changes.
data_spec.vintage: As released 2 October 2026 at 08:30 EDT; September preliminary estimate. Preserve this dated vintage.
data_spec.transform: Code reads the admitted Table B-1 seasonally adjusted change cells: goods-producing +18 and private service-providing +28. Code derives government change as Total nonfarm change (+29) minus Total private change (+46), yielding -17; independently reconcile against the differences of total-minus-private levels in August and September. The three plotted groups must sum to +29. Total private is a reconciliation subtotal, never an additional plotted component. No imputation.
data_spec.chart_form: Three horizontal diverging bars on one zero-centred axis, with explicit +18, +28 and -17 labels; annotate total nonfarm +29 separately. Label groups Private goods-producing, Private services, Government. Do not portray this as a detailed industry-sector chart.

data_spec.subtitle: Monthly change, thousands of jobs; seasonally adjusted; released 2 October 2026
data_spec.actual_estimate_forecast: Observed BLS preliminary employment estimates, not a forecast.
data_spec.missingness: No missingness in the selected admitted cells. If code cannot reconcile the derived government component, retain the exact source mismatch for repair rather than fill it.
data_spec.rights: BLS agency-authored official public-domain data; attribution in chart source line.
